A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and support reliable comparison of text, tables, figures, and appendices. v3 retains the scientific material through Appendix B; the removed pages are v2's NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original brain-response prediction experiments on NSD subjects 1, 2, 5, and 7, alongside attention analyses and generated-stimulus results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original NSD prediction experiments and the empirical analyses in Appendices A.1–A.4.

M1.justification: The transformer decoder, ROI and vertex queries, masking, training objective, and ensemble procedure are unchanged. Introducing the TBEn acronym and revising parameter-count estimates do not document an architecture or algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NSD subjects, image- and caption-based brain-response prediction tasks, and ROI-guided image-generation scenario. No dataset, population, or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: ridge regression, CLS and PCA regression, spatial-feature factorization, saliency-based integration, and the same routing variants. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes in Tables 1 and 3–6 decrease by roughly one quarter. This revises a reported experimental attribute, without establishing reruns or an actual architecture change. Splits, preprocessing, metrics, and training procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-size analysis, ROI-versus-vertex routing comparisons, layer ensemble analysis, attention selectivity, query similarity, and generated-image studies are retained with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain ten-fold cross-validation and Appendix A.3's averaging over twenty models using five seeds and four backbone layers. Removing the checklist adds no change to uncertainty reporting or subject-wise reporting practices.

E6.justification: Parameter-count entries change: Table 1 revises ridge regression from approximately 1200M to 900M and the ROI transformer from 37M to 28M; Table 4 revises the ensemble from 400M to 300M. Encoding accuracies, rankings, and appendix findings remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of attention, masking, the loss, and encoding accuracy are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about prediction accuracy, parameter efficiency, interpretability, and content-dependent routing as a candidate brain mechanism. The TBEn name does not alter their scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of routing granularity, backbone representations, and attention selectivity are unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning other recording techniques, modalities, and anatomical constraints; the removed checklist supplies no substantive additional scientific qualification.

D1.justification: Reported parameter totals are revised without an accompanying counting explanation. The architecture details, code-access statement, and Appendix B's NVIDIA L40s, storage, and GPU-hour disclosures remain unchanged. The checklist's separate promise of supplementary code is omitted.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and references 1–53 are unchanged. The relationship to prior encoding models, transformers, and BrainDiVE is retained.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 introduces the name Transformer Brain Encoder (TBEn), and the standalone NeurIPS checklist is removed. The main narrative, section order, and scientific appendices otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption is edited and reflowed to introduce TBEn. Scientific figure panels and table structures remain unchanged, including all appendix displays. The checklist's trailing pages are removed.

improvement.justification: The predictive evidence, scientific appendices, and substantive explanations are unchanged. The principal numerical revision lowers parameter-count estimates without explaining their calculation or counting basis, so the PDFs do not establish whether resource reporting became more accurate. Naming edits and removal of the largely redundant checklist have limited effects and do not resolve the overall quality direction.
